title_en: Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, and Zhou Jianguang v. Deqing Jinkunheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Zhang Pingping, Shen Jinlong, and Chen Lianying — dispute over third-party revocation action
ruling_gist_en: Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the subjects entitled to file a third-party revocation lawsuit shall be strictly limited to the two categories of third parties provided in the preceding two paragraphs of that article, namely those with independent claims and those without independent claims. It is impermissible to extend the subjects entitled to file a third-party revocation lawsuit to persons other than the two categories of third parties specified in Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, including an outsider who holds an ordinary creditor's right. If the original judgment is indeed erroneous, it may be corrected through the trial supervision procedure in accordance with the law.
keywords_en: Civil; Third-party revocation lawsuit; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Zhejiang Province; Natural person; Legal person; Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; Standing to file a third-party revocation lawsuit; Whether an ordinary creditor may file a third-party revocation lawsuit; Dismissal of claims; Dispute over equity transfer; False mediation; Ordinary creditor's right; Chen Lianying third-party revocation lawsuit dispute
full_text_en:
Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, Zhou Jianguang v. Deqing Jinhengkun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Zhang Pingping, Shen Jinlong, and Chen Lianying — dispute over a third-party revocation action

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the subjects entitled to file a third-party revocation action shall be strictly limited to the two types of third parties specified in the first two paragraphs of that Article, namely, those with an independent claim and those without an independent claim. The scope of subjects entitled to file a third-party revocation action shall not be expanded to include persons outside the case who hold ordinary creditor's rights beyond the two types of third parties specified in Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the original case is indeed erroneous, it may be corrected through the trial supervision procedure in accordance with law.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2017) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 319

Appellants (plaintiffs at first instance): Hu Bingguang, male, born November 11, 1954, Han ethnicity, residing in Wencheng County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaoyan, lawyer at Zhejiang Guanzhao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Jianfei, lawyer at Zhejiang Liuhe Law Firm.

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Hu Shaoliao (Hu Shao Liao), male, born September 13, 1953, nationality of the French Republic, residing in Seine Town, Ile-de-France Region, Marne Department, French Republic, postal code 77340 (77340 PON-TAULT COMBAUI.T FRANCE).

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaoyan, lawyer at Zhejiang Guanzhao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Jianfei, lawyer at Zhejiang Liuhe Law Firm.

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Zhou Duyuan, male, born February 11, 1929, Han ethnicity, residing in Wencheng County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaoyan, lawyer at Zhejiang Guanzhao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Jianfei, lawyer at Zhejiang Liuhe Law Firm.

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Jiang Meiyu, male, born July 20, 1958, Han ethnicity, residing in Wencheng County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaoyan, lawyer at Zhejiang Guanzhao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Haisheng, lawyer at Beijing Jiangshan Law Firm.

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Zhou Jianguang (Chou Chien Kuang), male, born November 7, 1963, nationality of the French Republic, residing in Melun City, French Republic, postal code 77000 (77000 MELUN FRANCE).

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaoyan, lawyer at Zhejiang Guanzhao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wan Jianfei, lawyer at Zhejiang Liuhe Law Firm.

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Deqing Jinhengkun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Deqing County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Shen Jinlong, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chi Weisong, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhuo Guangping, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Zhang Pingping, female, born August 30, 1982, Han ethnicity, residing in Deqing County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Chi Weisong, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhuo Guangping, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Shen Jinlong, male, born November 26, 1964, Han ethnicity, residing in Deqing County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Chi Weisong, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhuo Guangping, lawyer at Zhejiang Tiance Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Chen Lianying, female, born October 31, 1951, Han ethnicity, residing in Wencheng County, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

In the case of a third-party revocation action brought by appellants Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, and Zhou Jianguang (hereinafter referred to as "Hu Bingguang et al., five persons") against appellants Deqing Jinhengkun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (formerly Xinfu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as "Jinhengkun Company"), Zhang Pingping, Shen Jinlong, and respondent Chen Lianying, the Zhejiang High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as "Zhejiang High Court") rendered Civil Judgment No. 1 (2015) Zhe Chu Zi on September 27, 2016. Hu Bingguang et al. (five persons), Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong all objected to the first-instance judgment of the Zhejiang High Court and appealed to this Court. After this Court accepted the case and formed a collegial panel in accordance with law, a public hearing was conducted. The joint agents ad litem of Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, and Zhou Jianguang, Xu Xiaoyan and Wan Jianfei; the agent ad litem of Jiang Meiyu, Xu Xiaoyan, and Chen Haisheng; the legal representative of Jinhengkun Company and appellant Shen Jinlong; and the joint agents ad litem of Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, Chi Weisong and Zhuo Guangping, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Respondent Chen Lianying, after the summons for trial was served by public notice by this Court, failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons, and this Court proceeded with trial by default in accordance with law. The case is now concluded.

Hu Bingguang et al. (five persons) filed a lawsuit with the Zhejiang High Court, requesting: 1. To revoke the Civil Mediation Document No. 63 (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi of the Zhejiang High Court in accordance with law; 2. The litigation costs of this case to be borne by the defendants at first instance. Facts and reasons: Hu Bingguang et al. (five persons) are respectively lawful creditors of Chen Lianying. As confirmed by effective legal documents of the court, they have a total of approximately RMB 40 million in claims against Chen Lianying. Since Chen Lianying and her husband failed to perform the debts determined by the effective legal documents, Hu Bingguang et al. (five persons) have respectively applied for compulsory execution to the relevant courts. Chen Lianying, Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong had a dispute over equity transfer contract (hereinafter referred to as "the original case"). After trial at first instance by the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province (hereinafter referred to as "Hangzhou Intermediate Court"), Civil Judgment No. 10 (2012) Zhe Hang Shang Chu Zi was rendered, ordering Jinhengkun Company to pay Chen Lianying equity transfer consideration and investment funds of RMB 78,548,457.18 plus corresponding interest, and Zhang Pingping to pay Chen Lianying equity transfer consideration and investment funds of RMB 57,000,000 plus corresponding interest. Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping objected and appealed. During the second-instance proceedings, the parties reached a mediation agreement that neither party owed the other any amount, which was confirmed by the Zhejiang High Court in Civil Mediation Document No. 63 (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi. There is now sufficient evidence to prove that the parties to the original case maliciously colluded to evade debts and reached a false mediation agreement, which was unlawfully confirmed by the mediation document of the second-instance proceedings, seriously damaging the lawful rights and interests of Hu Bingguang et al. (five persons), and therefore should be revoked.

The Zhejiang High Court found the following facts at first instance: In the original case, Chen Lianying filed a lawsuit with the Hangzhou Intermediate Court on January 5, 2012, on the grounds that "on December 9, 2010, she transferred 32% of her equity in Hangzhou Zhongwang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'Zhongwang Company') to Jinhengkun Company at a price of RMB 143 million; on December 28 of the same year, she transferred the remaining 10% of her equity to Zhang Pingping at a price of RMB 57 million. After the procedures for the change of registration of the equity transfer were completed, Jinhengkun Company paid only RMB 38 million, and the remaining amount was not paid; Zhang Pingping paid nothing at all. Shen Jinlong, as the husband of Zhang Pingping, should bear joint repayment liability for Zhang Pingping's debts." The request was for an order: 1. Jinhengkun Company to pay equity transfer consideration and investment funds of RMB 110,338,410, plus interest from September 1, 2011, until the date of full payment (temporarily calculated as of July 1, 2012, as RMB 11,033,841); 2. Zhang Pingping and Shen Jinlong to pay equity transfer consideration and investment funds of RMB 57,000,000, plus interest from September 1, 2011, until the date of full payment (temporarily calculated as of July 1, 2012, as RMB 5,700,000); 3. Jinhengkun Company to pay an interest compensation of RMB 10,000,000 for the first three years.

After trial, the Hangzhou Intermediate Court found that on February 1, 2010, Chen Lianying, Xu Dingzhou, and Lin Yuanlin respectively transferred 7%, 23%, and 21% of their equity in Zhongwang Company to Ningbo Tianguan Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'Tianguan Company'). After the transfer, the equity structure of Zhongwang Company was: Tianguan Company contributed RMB 5.1 million, accounting for 51% of the registered capital; Chen Lianying contributed RMB 4.2 million, accounting for 42% of the registered capital; Lin Yuanlin contributed RMB 700,000, accounting for 7% of the registered capital. On December 9 of the same year, Tianguan Company and Lin Yuanlin respectively transferred 51% and 7% of their equity in Zhongwang Company to Jinhengkun Company. On the same day, Chen Lianying also signed an equity transfer agreement with Jinhengkun Company, transferring 32% of the 42% equity she held in Zhongwang Company to Jinhengkun Company at a price of RMB 3.2 million (no premium). The transfer price had been paid to Chen Lianying through Zhongwang Company on October 11, 2010. The transfer agreement also stated: As of November 30, 2010, Chen Lianying had actually invested RMB 163.2 million in Zhongwang Company (tentatively, subject to the audit report issued by the accounting firm entrusted by Jinhengkun Company) for the development and construction of Block Yu Zheng Gua Chu (2008) 09 and various preliminary works, including demolition. Of this actual investment amount, RMB 107.2 million was also transferred to Jinhengkun Company. Chen Lianying retained the remaining 10% equity and RMB 56 million in investment funds, which remained in Zhongwang Company and could not be withdrawn early, etc. Chen Lianying also issued a letter of undertaking to Jinhengkun Company, listing 10 debts and their treatment methods, confirming that apart from the 10 debts listed, Zhongwang Company had no other due or undue debts, and that if any debts other than the 10 listed were discovered in the future, they would be borne by Chen Lianying.

On December 28, 2010, Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and Chen Lianying signed a supplemental agreement, making corresponding changes to the payment time for the investment transfer price in addition to the originally agreed equity transfer price: RMB 13 million to be paid before January 15, 2011; RMB 2 million to be paid before February 2, 2011; RMB 28 million to be paid before April 2011. All investment funds would not bear interest or dividends before August 31, 2011. From September 1, 2011, to August 31, 2012, the remaining investment funds would bear interest at a monthly rate of 1%. Starting from September 1, 2011, an investment transfer payment of RMB 2 million would be made monthly. By July 1, 2012, regardless of whether the demolition was completed, all remaining investment transfer funds should be paid in full. The total investment amount and the amounts payable would be determined after audit as originally agreed. Funds actually used by Chen Lianying for the project demolition of Zhongwang Company would be recognized, and tax invoices were not required. Chen Lianying should complete the industrial and commercial registration for the transfer of 12% equity on December 28, 2010, and upon receipt of the above RMB 13 million, complete the industrial and commercial registration for the transfer of 20% equity. The supplemental agreement also stipulated that Chen Lianying would transfer her remaining 10% equity to Zhang Pingping, and the industrial and commercial registration should be completed before January 15, 2011; Zhang Pingping should pay Chen Lianying a transfer price of RMB 57 million (including RMB 1 million for the 10% equity transfer and RMB 56 million for the investment transfer) in accordance with the above time limits and conditions. On the same day, Jinhengkun Company issued a letter of undertaking, promising to compensate Chen Lianying RMB 10 million as interest for the first three years after Zhongwang Company completed the demolition and renovation of its World Trade Fabric City reconstruction and development project and after the project of Zhongwang Company was launched for sale. On January 17, 2011, both parties completed the industrial and commercial registration procedures for the equity transfer.

On June 21, 2011, Party A: Zhejiang Guogang Industrial Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'Guogang Company'), Party B: Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, Party C: Chen Lianying, and Party D: Chongqing Shennong Investment Group Co., Ltd. and Zhongwang Company signed a payment agreement (hereinafter referred to as the 'Four-Party Agreement'), stipulating that the actual investment by Party C, Chen Lianying, refers to the expenses incurred by her for Zhongwang Company's land, demolition, and normal operating expenses, deducted from expenses unrelated to Zhongwang Company's land, demolition, and normal operations during the period when Party C held the equity (including Zhongwang Company's debts, guarantee liabilities, tort liabilities, and administrative penalties assumed by Zhongwang Company). The preliminary determination of the actual investment amount was RMB 187 million (including RMB 48.31 million recorded in Yang Bufeng's off-book accounts), but it was subject to an audit jointly entrusted to Zhonghui Certified Public Accountants (hereinafter referred to as 'Zhonghui Firm'), with the final amount to be determined by the audit conclusion. Party A, Guogang Company, would, based on the audit conclusion, replace Party B, Jinhengkun Company, and Zhang Pingping, to pay the outstanding transfer price to Party C, Chen Lianying, including RMB 30 million before July 5, 2011, and RMB 20 million before July 15, 2011... The agreement would take effect upon being signed and sealed by all four parties, Party A, B, C, and D, and upon Party A's actual performance of the above RMB 50 million payment obligation. The 'Four-Party Agreement' also stipulated other related matters. After the agreement was signed, Guogang Company paid Chen Lianying a total of RMB 17 million between June 20 and August 9, 2011, and did not make further payments for the remaining amount. On August 5, 2011, Guogang Company notified Chen Lianying in writing, clearly stating that it was unable to perform the RMB 50 million payment obligation, that the conditions for the effectiveness of the 'Four-Party Agreement' were not met, that the agreement was not effective and was void, and requiring Chen Lianying to assert her corresponding rights against Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping.

The Hangzhou Intermediate Court further found that on January 17, 2011, Chen Lianying instructed Jinhengkun Company to pay RMB 13 million to Zhou Make, and on January 30 of the same year, instructed Jinhengkun Company to pay RMB 25 million to Lin Yuanlin. Chen Lianying acknowledged that these two payments should be deducted from the transfer price payable by Jinhengkun Company. In addition, according to Civil Judgment No. 504 (2011) Hang Yu Min Chu Zi rendered by the Yuhang District People's Court of Hangzhou on May 21, 2012, Zhongwang Company, in a property damage compensation dispute, was ordered to compensate Hangzhou Yiqun Silk Co., Ltd. RMB 5,240,670.82, pay appraisal fees of RMB 73,600, preservation fees of RMB 5,000, and bear the case acceptance fee of RMB 44,572. During the trial of the original case, the Hangzhou Intermediate Court, upon Chen Lianying's application, entrusted Zhejiang Weining Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'Weining Company') to conduct a special audit of Chen Lianying and her husband Yang Bufeng's equity investment and debt investment in Zhongwang Company. After the audit, the firm issued Special Audit Report No. 323 (2013) Zhe Wei Hui Shen Zi, with the audit conclusion stating: As of December 31, 2010, the investment of Chen Lianying (including her husband Yang Bufeng) in Zhongwang Company was as follows: 1. Off-book payment of equity transfer consideration of RMB 110 million; 2. Payments made by Chen Lianying within Zhongwang Company's accounts totaling RMB 60,345,200; 3. Payments made by Chen Lianying on behalf of Zhongwang Company but not yet recorded in Zhongwang Company's accounts totaling RMB 7,567,100. The audit report also explained other related matters.

After trial, the Hangzhou Intermediate Court held that the equity transfer agreement between Chen Lianying and Jinhengkun Company, the supplemental agreement between Chen Lianying, Jinhengkun Company, and Zhang Pingping, and the above 'Four-Party Agreement' were all valid. Since Guogang Company failed to fully perform its payment obligation to Chen Lianying within the time limit and in the amount specified in the 'Four-Party Agreement' and, after paying part of the amount, explicitly informed Chen Lianying that it would no longer perform the payment obligation, the agreement, as per its terms, ceased to be the basis for settling the investment and equity transfer consideration among the parties. The equity transfer matters between Jinhengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and Chen Lianying should be performed in accordance with the equity transfer agreement and the supplemental agreement. Chen Lianying had performed her contractual obligations by transferring her equity in Zhongwang Company to Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping as agreed. Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping should also pay Chen Lianying the investment and equity transfer consideration as agreed. The audit report confirmed that Chen Lianying's (including her husband's) total investment in Zhongwang Company was RMB 177,912,300. Although the off-book payment of RMB 110 million did not enter Zhongwang Company, it constituted consideration for Chen Lianying's subsequent transfer of Zhongwang Company equity to Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping, and the objections raised by Jinhengkun Company and Zhang Pingping as to the relevance of this portion of funds to the case were untenable. The RMB 38 million paid by Jinhengkun Company on behalf of Chen Lianying to Zhou Make and Lin Yuanlin should be deducted from the payable transfer consideration. According to the commitment letter issued by Chen Lianying to Jinhengkun Company on December 9, 2010, ...

letter of undertaking issued by Zhongwang Company, the compensation of RMB 5,240,670.82 and appraisal fees of RMB 73,600, preservation fees of RMB 5,000, and case acceptance fees of RMB 44,572 that Zhongwang Company was required to pay to Hangzhou Yiqun Silk Co., Ltd. pursuant to Civil Judgment (2011) Hang Yu Min Chu Zi No. 504 should also be borne by Chen Lianying and thus deducted. Accordingly, Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping should pay Chen Lianying a total transfer price of RMB 134,548,457.18, of which Zhang Pingping should pay RMB 57 million (including an investment of RMB 56 million) and interest of RMB 5.7 million, and Jin Hengkun Company should pay RMB 78,548,457.18 and interest of RMB 7,854,845.71, with subsequent interest calculated until the date of full payment. As for Chen Lianying's claim that Jin Hengkun Company should pay an additional compensation of RMB 10 million for the first three years' interest, since the condition for payment stipulated in the letter of undertaking issued by Jin Hengkun Company was not satisfied, this claim was not supported. This case is a dispute over equity transfer, and Shen Jinlong is not a party to the contract. Based on the principle of privity of contract, Chen Lianying's request that Shen Jinlong be jointly and severally liable for the payment of the equity transfer price and investment of RMB 57 million and interest was not supported. In accordance with Articles 8, 60, 93, and 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Zhe Hang Shang Chu Zi No. 10 on October 25, 2013, as follows: 1. Jin Hengkun Company shall pay Chen Lianying the equity transfer investment of RMB 78,548,457.18 within ten days after the judgment takes effect, and pay interest on that amount at a monthly rate of 1% from September 1, 2011, to the date of payment specified in the effective judgment, with a provisional calculation to July 1, 2012, of RMB 7,854,845.71. 2. Zhang Pingping shall pay Chen Lianying the equity transfer investment of RMB 57,000,000 within ten days after the judgment takes effect, and pay interest on that amount at a monthly rate of 1% from September 1, 2011, to the date of payment specified in the effective judgment, with a provisional calculation to July 1, 2012, of RMB 5,700,000. 3. Chen Lianying's other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,012,161 and the property preservation application fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 1,017,161, shall be borne by Chen Lianying in the amount of RMB 235,689, by Jin Hengkun Company in the amount of RMB 452,852, and by Zhang Pingping in the amount of RMB 328,620.

After the judgment was announced, Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping appealed to the Zhejiang High People's Court. During the second-instance proceedings, Jin Hengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, Shen Jinlong, and Chen Lianying voluntarily reached the following mediation agreement, requesting approval: (1) All parties confirm that Chen Lianying's actual investment in Zhongwang Company for the preliminary demolition work of Plot 09, used for the development, construction, and demolition of the land block designated as Yu Zheng Gua Chu (2008) 09, amounted to RMB 79,319,894.47. (2) In accordance with the agreement or Chen Lianying's commitment, the following total of RMB 60,363,842.80 shall be deducted from the equity transfer price: (a) RMB 43,363,842.80 already confirmed in Civil Judgment (2012) Zhe Hang Shang Chu Zi No. 10; (b) RMB 17 million paid by Guogang Company on behalf of Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping. After deduction, the remaining equity transfer price to be paid by Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping to Chen Lianying is RMB 18,956,051.67. (3) The relevant payments already made by Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping to Chen Lianying of RMB 16,482,413, and the interest arrears confirmed by Chen Lianying of RMB 4,952,000, totaling RMB 21,434,413, shall be fully offset against the remaining equity transfer price of RMB 18,956,051.67 and interest. (4) Between Jin Hengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, Shen Jinlong on one side, and Chen Lianying on the other, all debts and credits related to this equity transfer and previous relevant matters (including all contents of items (1), (2), and (3) of this mediation agreement) are fully settled, with no further disputes. (5) The first-instance litigation fees shall be enforced according to the original judgment; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,012,161, reduced by half to RMB 506,080.5, shall be borne by Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping. Upon review, the Zhejiang High People's Court found that the above agreement complied with legal provisions and issued Civil Mediation Letter (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63 on April 4, 2014, confirming it.

In this case, based on the parties' statements and the evidence examined and confirmed, the Zhejiang High People's Court found the following facts: Hu Bingguang and four others had disputes with Chen Lianying and a third party, Yang Bufeng, over private lending relationships, which were litigated separately. After trial by the relevant people's courts, it was confirmed that Hu Bingguang and the four others had claims against Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng, and the civil judgments or mediation letters determined that Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng should bear corresponding liabilities, including: 1. In the dispute over private lending between Hu Bingguang and Wu Lianghong, Zheng Tingyu, Zhongwang Company, and Yang Bufeng, the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2011) Zhe Hang Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 43 on July 25, 2012, ordering Wu Lianghong to repay Hu Bingguang the principal of RMB 18.43 million and pay overdue interest of RMB 1.62 million (calculated until April 18, 2012, with subsequent overdue interest calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% on the principal of RMB 18.43 million until the date the judgment takes effect); Zheng Tingyu and Yang Bufeng were jointly and severally liable for the above loan principal and overdue interest. After the judgment was announced, Wu Lianghong and Zheng Tingyu appealed, and the Zhejiang High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Zhe Shang Wai Zhong Zi No. 60 on December 12, 2012, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. During the enforcement of that case, Chen Lianying issued a written commitment to assume joint and several liability for the above debts. 2. In the dispute over private lending between Hu Shaoliao and Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying, the Huzhou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Huzhou Intermediate Court) rendered Civil Judgment (2012) Zhe Hu Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 14 on November 13, 2012, ordering Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying to jointly repay Hu Shaoliao the loan principal of RMB 6,779,120 and interest of RMB 6,779,119, totaling RMB 13,558,239, and pay interest on the overdue principal of RMB 6,779,120 (at a monthly rate of 2% from May 1, 2012, until the date of full payment). This judgment has become legally effective. 3. In the dispute over private lending between Zhou Duyuan and Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying, the parties reached a mediation agreement during the proceedings, whereby Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying would repay Zhou Duyuan RMB 5,083,900 (including principal of RMB 3,603,600, interest of RMB 592,300, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 888,000) before June 30, 2013, with RMB 1.2 million to be paid before June 10, 2012, and RMB 3,883,900 to be paid before June 30, 2013; in the event of default, Zhou Duyuan could apply for enforcement for RMB 5,675,900 (including principal of RMB 3,603,600, interest of RMB 592,300, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 1.48 million). The Huzhou Intermediate Court issued Civil Mediation Letter (2012) Zhe Hu Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 8 on May 29, 2012, confirming the mediation agreement reached between the parties. 4. In the dispute over private lending between Jiang Meiyu and Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying, the parties reached a mediation agreement during the proceedings, whereby Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying would repay Jiang Meiyu RMB 1,596,000 (including principal of RMB 1,150,000, interest of RMB 230,000, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 216,000) before June 30, 2013, with RMB 400,000 to be paid before June 10, 2012, and RMB 1,196,000 to be paid before June 30, 2013; in the event of default, Jiang Meiyu could apply for enforcement for RMB 1,738,000 (including principal of RMB 1,150,000, interest of RMB 230,000, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 358,000). The Huzhou Intermediate Court rendered Civil Mediation Letter (2012) Zhe Hu Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 9 on May 29, 2012, confirming the mediation agreement reached between the parties. 5. In the dispute over private lending between Zhou Jianguang and Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying, the parties reached a mediation agreement during the proceedings, whereby Yang Bufeng and Chen Lianying would repay Zhou Jianguang RMB 1,596,000 (including principal of RMB 1,150,000, interest of RMB 230,000, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 216,000) before June 30, 2013, with RMB 400,000 to be paid before June 10, 2012, and RMB 1,196,000 to be paid before June 30, 2013; in the event of default, Zhou Jianguang could apply for enforcement for RMB 1,738,000 (including principal of RMB 1,150,000, interest of RMB 230,000, and overdue repayment interest of RMB 358,000). The Huzhou Intermediate Court issued Civil Mediation Letter (2012) Zhe Hu Shang Wai Chu Zi No. 13 on May 29, 2012, confirming the mediation agreement reached between the parties. After the above civil judgments or mediation letters became effective, Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng failed to perform their debts as scheduled. Hu Bingguang and the four others accordingly applied for enforcement to the Hangzhou Intermediate Court and Huzhou Intermediate Court respectively, but Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng lacked executable property. During the trial of the original case (i.e., (2012) Zhe Hang Shang Chu Zi No. 10), the Hangzhou Intermediate Court and Huzhou Intermediate Court respectively issued notices of assistance in enforcement to Jin Hengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, etc., stating that if Jin Hengkun Company, Zhang Pingping, and others were found by the court to be required to pay equity transfer price to Chen Lianying, they were required to assist in freezing the corresponding amounts of the debts owed by Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng to Hu Bingguang and the four others, and to be extracted by the court according to law. At the same time, the Huzhou Intermediate Court also issued a notice of assistance in enforcement to the Hangzhou Intermediate Court, stating that if Chen Lianying prevailed in the original equity transfer dispute case and applied for enforcement to realize her claims, it requested assistance in extracting the corresponding amounts of the debts owed by Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng to Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, and Zhou Jianguang.

Separately, it was found that, as approved by the administrative department for industry and commerce, the enterprise name of Xinfu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. was changed to Deqing Jin Hengkun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in June 2014.

The Zhejiang High People's Court held that, among the plaintiffs in this case, Hu Shaoliao and Zhou Jianguang are nationals of the French Republic. Pursuant to Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, this case is a foreign-related civil action. Regarding the jurisdiction of the case, pursuant to Article 56(3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a third-party revocation action shall be filed with the people's court that rendered the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation letter. Since the effective mediation letter involved in this case was rendered by the Zhejiang High People's Court, the Zhejiang High People's Court has jurisdiction over this case according to law. Regarding the application of law, during the trial, all parties present agreed to apply the law of the People's Republic of China to the trial of this case, and this was confirmed.

Based on the parties' submissions and defense, the disputed issue in this case is whether the lawsuit filed by Hu Bingguang and the four others meets the conditions for a third-party revocation action. In accordance with the spirit of Article 56(3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 292 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Zhejiang High People's Court analyzes and determines as follows:

I. Whether Hu Bingguang and the four others meet the subject conditions for a third-party revocation action.

According to legal provisions, the plaintiff in a third-party revocation action shall be a third party who was unable to participate in the original lawsuit due to reasons not attributable to themselves, including a third party with an independent claim and a third party without an independent claim. Generally speaking, an outsider whose civil rights and interests may be harmed by the outcome of the original case is a qualified plaintiff for a third-party revocation action. However, ordinary claims are not protected by third-party revocation actions in principle, meaning that ordinary creditors of a party in the original case generally cannot initiate a third-party revocation action as plaintiffs. However, if the parties in the original case maliciously collude to engage in false litigation, ordinary creditors can initiate a third-party revocation action as victims of false litigation. In addition, claims that are specifically protected by law, including claims with statutory priority rights and claims with statutory revocation rights, may also be protected by third-party revocation actions.

In this case, Hu Bingguang and the four others only have ordinary claims against Chen Lianying (and Yang Bufeng) based on private lending relationships. They do not have an independent claim with respect to the subject matter of the original lawsuit. The outcome of the original case may have a certain de facto interest in whether Hu Bingguang and the four others can realize their ordinary claims in the court enforcement proceedings. However, this type of de facto interest is not equivalent to a legal interest. Therefore, generally speaking, Hu Bingguang and the four others are not third parties in the original case. As ordinary creditors of Chen Lianying, whether they have the plaintiff's qualification in this case should also be examined in conjunction with the substantive conditions of the third-party revocation action, i.e., whether the parties in the original lawsuit maliciously colluded to engage in false litigation, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of Hu Bingguang and the four others, or whether the ordinary claims of Hu Bingguang and the four others fall within the scope of claims specifically protected by law.

II. Whether this case meets the substantive conditions for a third-party revocation action.

Hu Bingguang and the four others argued in the lawsuit that Chen Lianying, Jin Hengkun Company, and Zhang Pingping maliciously colluded to reach a false mediation agreement in the second-instance proceedings of the original case, abandoning huge claims, thereby constituting false litigation and harming the legitimate rights and interests of numerous creditors, including Hu Bingguang and the four others. Although this assertion lacks direct evidence, it should be adopted based on a comprehensive review of all facts and evidence of the original lawsuit.

From the basic facts of the original case, in July 2009, Wu Lianghong, the original shareholder of Zhongwang Company, transferred 28% and 23% of its shares to Lin Yuanlin and Xu Dingzhou respectively. In February 2010, Xu Dingzhou and Lin Yuanlin transferred 23% and 21% of the shares to Tianguan Company respectively. In December of the same year, Lin Yuanlin transferred the remaining 7% of the shares to Jin Hengkun Company. According to the audit report of Weining Company, Chen Lianying had signed a "Shareholding Agreement" with Lin Yuanlin and Xu Dingzhou on July 6, 2009, in which Lin Yuanlin and Xu Dingzhou were only "nominee shareholders" of the above shares, and thus the true rights holders of those shares were Chen Lianying. During the series of equity transfers of Zhongwang Company, the registered capital of RMB 10 million did not change. Since the company signed a state-owned construction land use right transfer contract with the Yuhang Branch of the Hangzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources in March 2008, acquiring the corresponding land block (referred to as Plot 09 in the original case) in a "raw land" manner and through listing for the construction of the "World Trade Fabric City Market," and when carrying out demolition and compensation work for the "World Trade Fabric City Market" and external property owners (i.e., the various preliminary work for the development, construction, and demolition of Plot 09 as referred to in the relevant contracts of the original case), the relevant shareholders made substantial capital investments, thereby forming claims against Zhongwang Company. When Chen Lianying (through Lin Yuanlin and Xu Dingzhou) acquired 51% of the shares from Wu Lianghong, she also acquired Wu Lianghong's claims against Zhongwang Company. Subsequently, when Chen Lianying transferred 42% of the shares to Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping, the transfer also included her claims against Zhongwang Company. However, based on the existing evidence, it can be determined that when Chen Lianying (through Xu Dingzhou and Lin Yuanlin) transferred 51% of the shares to Tianguan Company in February 2010, the corresponding claims were not transferred to Tianguan Company. In December 2010, when Tianguan Company transferred its 51% of the shares to Jin Hengkun Company, although both parties confirmed the simultaneous transfer of RMB 128.3 million in claims, based on the audit report issued by Zhonghui Firm and the analysis of a series of contracts and agreements signed by the relevant parties, these claims were formed by Tianguan Company after it acquired 51% of the shares from Chen Lianying (through Xu Dingzhou and Lin Yuanlin) and directly invested in Zhongwang Company, none of which were claims transferred from Chen Lianying. Therefore, when Chen Lianying transferred rights to Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping in a "equity plus claims" manner, the claims portion consisted of the claims she had acquired from Wu Lianghong (i.e., the "off-book payment of equity transfer price" as referred to in the audit report of Weining Company) and the claims formed by her direct investment in Zhongwang Company (i.e., the "payments recorded in Zhongwang Company's books" and "payments made by Chen Lianying on behalf of Zhongwang Company but not yet recorded by Zhongwang Company" as referred to in the audit report of Weining Company). After Jin Hengkun Company and Zhang Pingping acquired such equity and claims, they should pay corresponding consideration.

According to the audit report of Weining Company, Chen Lianying's total investment in the project (i.e., the total amount of creditor's rights transferred to Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping) was RMB 177,912,300. However, in Article 1 of the mediation agreement of the original case, the parties determined that Chen Lianying's "actual funds invested in Zhongwang Company for the development, construction, and demolition of Plot 09" was only RMB 79,319,894.47, a discrepancy of over RMB 98 million. It should be noted that the audit report of Weining Company was issued by the court of first instance in the original case upon a party's application for a legally commissioned audit during the proceedings. The auditing institution and auditors had the relevant qualifications, the audit procedures were lawful, and the audit conclusions should be admitted as evidence unless there were obvious insufficient grounds or other circumstances that rendered them inadmissible after cross-examination. However, in the proceedings of the original case, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping did not provide sufficient evidence to overturn the above audit conclusions. In the proceedings of this case, the Zhejiang High People's Court ordered Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping to explain the total amount of creditor's rights as determined in Article 1 of the mediation agreement of the original case. Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping provided two calculation methods, but neither method had a basis and could not be accepted: First, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping claimed that, according to the audit report of Weining Company, as of December 31, 2010, the development cost of the "World Trade Fabric City" project was RMB 296,806,494.70. After deducting the accounts payable balance of RMB 21,408,600, the actual total cost was RMB 275,397,894.70, of which RMB 12.83 million was invested by Tianguan Company, while Jin Hengkui Company invested RMB 67,778,000 from October to December 2010 after acquiring the equity. According to the formula "actual total cost of the World Trade Fabric City project - funds invested by Tianguan Company - funds invested by Jin Hengkui Company," Chen Lianying's actual investment was RMB 79,319,894.70, which roughly corresponded to the amount in Article 1 of the mediation agreement. However, this calculation method by Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping only extracted a portion of the audit report of Weining Company, using the development cost of the "World Trade Fabric City" project as the base, which severed the inherent relationship between this data and other data, lacking scientific validity. In fact, according to the audit report of Weining Company, as of December 31, 2010, Zhongwang Company's total book assets were RMB 356,126,208.60, including monetary funds of RMB 85,907.19, other receivables of RMB 56,470,806.69, and inventory of RMB 298,181,774.70 (of which the development cost of the Fabric City project was RMB 296,806,494.70)... Clearly, the development cost of the "World Trade Fabric City" project was only part of the "inventory" within Zhongwang Company's total assets, which also included other substantial assets. These assets were accumulated from Zhongwang Company's shareholders' past investments and were also related to "the development, construction, demolition, and other preliminary work of Plot 09." There was no evidence that these assets had been separately recovered by Chen Lianying or others. In the above calculation method, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping stripped these assets from Zhongwang Company's total assets, which obviously lacked a basis. Their equation of the funds incurred for "development, construction, demolition, and other preliminary work of Plot 09" with "the development cost of the World Trade Fabric City project" was also logically untenable. Second, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping also claimed that if the audit conclusion in the Weining Company report that Chen Lianying's total investment was RMB 177,912,300 was taken as the base, the following four items should be deducted: First, the RMB 110 million consideration paid by Chen Lianying to Wu Lianghong for the acquisition of 51% equity included a premium of RMB 19.04 million and an introduction fee, interest, intangible assets, etc., of RMB 5.55 million, totaling RMB 24.59 million; Second, among the funds Tianguan Company invested in Zhongwang Company, at least RMB 13.45 million was used by Chen Lianying to repay her own debts; Third, among the accounts payable of Zhongwang Company of RMB 21.41 million in the Weining Company audit report, RMB 18.65 million was an undisclosed debt of Chen Lianying, which, according to a commitment letter issued by Chen Lianying on December 9, 2010, should be borne by her; Fourth, Chen Lianying had promised Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping that her son Yang Xipeng and daughter-in-law Hu Aimin would use the land use right of Hangzhou Pengwei Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pengwei Company) as collateral for a loan of RMB 30 million, guaranteeing that it would be used for Pengwei Company; otherwise, the amount would be deducted from the transfer payment between her and Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping. However, the RMB 30 million was not actually used for Pengwei Company, resulting in Pengwei Company's assets being auctioned by the court, causing asset losses of RMB 10 million, so the total of RMB 43 million should be deducted. The cumulative amount of the above four deduction items was approximately RMB 99 million, so as of December 31, 2010, Chen Lianying's investment balance was approximately RMB 78 million, which also roughly corresponded to the amount in Article 1 of the mediation agreement. However, according to the logic of the mediation agreement in the original case, Article 1 of that agreement addressed the total amount of Chen Lianying's investment, while deduction items were covered by Article 2. By including the above four deduction items in Article 1, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping violated the logic and wording of the mediation agreement in the original case. Moreover, among the four deduction items they claimed, apart from the third item involving Zhongwang Company's accounts payable of RMB 18,208,600, which might need to be borne by Chen Lianying personally according to her commitment letter of December 9, 2010, and deducted from the transfer payment, the deduction of the remaining items lacked a basis and could not be supported: First, although the transfer payment made by Chen Lianying to Wu Lianghong included a premium and other intangible asset fees, these amounts were the actual consideration paid by Chen Lianying. Furthermore, when she later transferred the equity (creditor's rights) to Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping, the parties only agreed that the equity part would be transferred "without premium," but no such agreement was made regarding the transfer of the creditor's rights. Therefore, including the "premium" and other fees actually paid to Wu Lianghong in the transfer scope did not violate the contract or legal provisions. Second, according to the audit report of Weining Company, part of the funds invested by Tianguan Company in Zhongwang Company was indeed used by Chen Lianying to repay her own debts, but Weining Company had already deducted these amounts under "payments made within Chen Lianying's accounts" during the audit. By including them again as deduction items in the second calculation method, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping were clearly unjustified. Finally, regarding the RMB 30 million debt of Yang Xipeng and Hu Aimin to the Yuhang Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., this was covered by the "Four-Party Agreement." Since the "Four-Party Agreement" never became effective, it was not binding on the four parties. Therefore, Jin Hengkui Company's and Zhang Pingping's claim for deduction of this debt and the alleged losses lacked a contractual basis. Even if the relevant provisions of the "Four-Party Agreement" were legally effective, there was no evidence that Yang Xipeng and Hu Aimin did not use the RMB 30 million loan for Pengwei Company, so Chen Lianying was not obligated to bear that amount under the agreement. Based on the above, the two calculation methods of Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping were untenable, and the content of Article 1 of the mediation agreement in the original case was clearly inconsistent with the facts. As for the remaining clauses of the mediation agreement, which involved issues such as deduction of amounts and debt offset, they were all based on Article 1 of the mediation agreement. Given that the authenticity of Article 1 could not be confirmed, regardless of whether the remaining clauses were true, the agreement as a whole lacked factual and legal basis.

In fact, as rational economic actors, both Chen Lianying and Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping should have had a correct understanding of the most basic elements of the contract, such as the subject matter and price, when signing the equity (creditor's rights) transfer contract. The estimated transfer price would generally not deviate significantly from the actual amount. In fact, the total amount of Chen Lianying's investment (i.e., the amount of creditor's rights transferred) stated in the equity transfer agreement and other relevant documents of the original case was much higher than the amount specified in Article 1 of the mediation agreement of the original case, but was close to the audit conclusion of Weining Company. In the proceedings of the original case, Chen Lianying's first-instance claim amount, including principal and interest, was as high as RMB 170 million. After deducting relevant items, the first-instance judgment supported over RMB 149 million. When the Zhejiang High People's Court mediated at the second instance, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping, based on their claims for deductions and offsets, had also agreed to pay a transfer price of RMB 40 million to RMB 45 million. However, without any significant change in the basic facts alleged by the parties, the parties ultimately reached a so-called "all creditor's rights and debts have been settled" mediation agreement and requested the court to confirm it. This conduct was inconsistent with common sense and gave ample reason to doubt the authenticity of the content of the mediation agreement.

Based on the above, the authenticity of the content of the mediation agreement in the original case cannot be confirmed. Chen Lianying, while owing substantial debts to others, gave up her due creditor's rights in the mediation agreement, demonstrating clear bad faith. With respect to the fact that Chen Lianying owed substantial debts to others, Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping should have known subjectively; the relevant court had even served a notice of assistance in enforcement on them, but they still entered into the above mediation agreement with Chen Lianying, which can hardly be considered an act of good faith. Even if it is not determined in this case that Chen Lianying and Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping maliciously colluded to reach a false mediation agreement, the mediation agreement should still be considered to fall within the scope of the creditor's right of revocation under Article 74 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Since the mediation agreement had a negative impact on the normal realization of claims by Chen Lianying's creditors, including Hu Bingguang and the other four, and harmed their civil rights and interests, the confirmation of the civil mediation document (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63 by the Zhejiang High People's Court was erroneous. According to the relevant provisions, this case meets the substantive conditions for a third-party revocation action.

III. Regarding whether the case meets the procedural conditions for a third-party revocation action

A third-party revocation action must primarily satisfy two procedural conditions: First, the plaintiff must not have participated in the original case proceedings due to reasons not attributable to him or her; second, the plaintiff must file the action within six months from the date he or she knew or should have known that his or her civil rights and interests were harmed. As for the first procedural condition, the plaintiff's failure to participate in the original case proceedings refers to the plaintiff not becoming a third party in the original case, not to the failure to actually participate in the process of the original case proceedings. As creditors of Chen Lianying, Hu Bingguang and the other four could not have participated in the original case as third parties during the first-instance proceedings. During the second-instance proceedings, they were also unaware of the fact that the parties in the original case had reached a false mediation agreement. Therefore, they were not subjectively at fault for not becoming third parties in the original case. As for the second procedural condition, Hu Bingguang and the other four jointly submitted a complaint to the Zhejiang High People's Court on April 1, 2015, to initiate this case. There is no evidence to prove that they already knew more than six months earlier that the content of the second-instance mediation document of the original case had harmed their rights. Therefore, the claim by Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong that Hu Bingguang and the other four had exceeded the six-month period for filing the action lacks a basis and is not accepted. This case meets the procedural conditions for a third-party revocation action.

In summary, this case meets the conditions for a third-party revocation action, and the second-instance mediation document of the original case should be revoked in accordance with the law. After the mediation document is revoked, the first-instance judgment naturally does not take effect, and the equity (creditor's rights) transfer dispute between the parties in the original case should be resolved through the corresponding litigation procedures anew. If Chen Lianying, as the plaintiff in the original case, fails to actively pursue her rights through normal litigation procedures after this judgment takes effect, Hu Bingguang and the other four may exercise the right of subrogation under Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and claim rights in their own name. After discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee of the Zhejiang High People's Court, the court, in accordance with Article 56, Article 92, and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 292, 294, and 300 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby renders the following judgment: Revoke the civil mediation document (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63 of the Zhejiang High People's Court. The case acceptance fee of RMB 241,800 shall be jointly borne by Chen Lianying, Jin Hengkui Company, and Zhang Pingping.

Hu Bingguang, the other four, as well as Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, all refused to accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to this court.

Hu Bingguang and the other four appealed, requesting: (1) While upholding the result of the first-instance judgment, correct the errors in the finding of facts and application of law in the first-instance judgment. (2) While upholding the first-instance judgment's result of "revoking the civil mediation document (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63," order a retrial of case (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63 or instruct the Zhejiang High People's Court to retry it. (3) The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by Chen Lianying, Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong. Facts and reasons: 1. The first-instance judgment's failure to determine that "Chen Lianying and Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping maliciously colluded to reach a false mediation agreement" was erroneous and should be corrected. Regardless of whether Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping subjectively reached the false mediation agreement solely to assist Chen Lianying in evading personal debts or also for their own improper interests, it should be determined as malicious collusion to obstruct enforcement through a false settlement. 2. The first-instance judgment's failure to find the fact that "Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping paid RMB 38 million to Chen Lianying's specific associates through specific connections" was an error in fact-finding and should be corrected. The letter from the Wencheng County Public Security Bureau to the Huzhou Intermediate People's Court and other related evidence indicated that the fact that Chen Lianying, Jin Hengkui Company, and Zhang Pingping made private payments through specific connections after reaching the false mediation agreement had reached a high degree of probability, sufficient to form inner conviction in any reasonable person. The Zhejiang High People's Court's failure to find this was clearly improper. 3. The first-instance judgment's statement that "after the mediation document is revoked, the first-instance judgment naturally does not take effect, and the equity (creditor's rights) transfer dispute between the parties in the original case should be resolved through the corresponding litigation procedures anew. If Chen Lianying fails to actively pursue her rights through normal litigation procedures after this judgment takes effect, the plaintiffs in this case may exercise the right of subrogation and claim rights in their own name" was an error in the application of law. The Zhejiang High People's Court should retry case (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63. The reason the Zhejiang High People's Court revoked the original mediation agreement was that the mediation agreement was indeed erroneous. According to the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and its judicial interpretations, the Zhejiang High People's Court should have ex officio retried the case. Although the first-instance judgment in the original case did not take effect due to the appeal, this does not mean that the first-instance proceedings of the original case ceased to exist. After the second-instance mediation document of the original case was revoked, a situation arose where the Zhejiang High People's Court had not rendered any ruling on the second-instance litigation between the parties in the original case. The Zhejiang High People's Court should have continued the second-instance trial of the original case or conducted a retrial.

Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong appealed, requesting: Revoke the first-instance judgment and remand for retrial, or after further investigation of the facts, amend the judgment to dismiss the lawsuit or reject all claims of Hu Bingguang and the other four in the first instance. Facts and reasons: 1. Hu Bingguang and the other four are not third parties with independent claims in the original case, nor do they have any legal interest in the outcome of the original case. Although there is some factual connection, they cannot be considered third parties without independent claims. They are not qualified plaintiffs under the third-party revocation action. The first-instance judgment's use of so-called substantive conditions to infer that Hu Bingguang and the other four met the standing requirements for a third-party revocation action was baseless, violated Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and improperly expanded the scope of plaintiffs eligible for a third-party revocation action. 2. Hu Bingguang and the other four claim that their harmed rights are non-specific ordinary monetary claims, which do not fall within the scope of civil rights and interests covered by the third-party revocation action and should not be included in the scope of the third-party revocation action procedure. 3. The first-instance judgment's finding that this case meets the procedural conditions for a third-party revocation action was erroneous. This case falls under the circumstance where the failure to participate in the original case proceedings was attributable to Hu Bingguang and the other four. From the outset, they believed that the trial of this case had factual or legal significance for them, but they neither applied to participate in the proceedings during the first and second instances nor submitted evidence that they had applied to participate as third parties and were rejected by the court or other reasons not attributable to them for not participating. Therefore, this case should be considered as a situation where the third parties themselves were responsible for not participating in the original case proceedings. Hu Bingguang and the other four did not file the action within six months from the date they "should have known." They exceeded the statutory six-month period, and their lawsuit does not meet the procedural conditions and should be dismissed. 4. The first-instance judgment's finding that this case meets the substantive conditions for a third-party revocation action was erroneous and involved exceeding or substituting the trial authority of the second instance in the original case. 5. Hu Bingguang and the other four's allegation that Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping privately paid Chen Lianying RMB 38 million was seriously false, and there was no falsity in the mediation agreement of the original case.

In response to the appeal of Hu Bingguang and the other four, Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong orally argued: The appeal of Hu Bingguang and the other four lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. Specific opinions are consistent with the appeal opinions.

In response to the appeal of Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, Hu Bingguang and the other four argued: 1. Hu Bingguang and the other four meet the standing requirements for a third-party revocation action. The first-instance judgment in this case has already found that Hu Bingguang and the other four, based on effective court judgments or rulings, have creditor's rights against Chen Lianying and Yang Bufeng. These creditor's rights are civil rights and interests protected by state compulsory enforcement. By giving up a substantial amount of creditor's rights in the mediation agreement with Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping, Chen Lianying used the mediation agreement to transfer property and evade enforcement, thereby preventing Hu Bingguang and the other four from exercising their right of revocation. In such circumstances, they should be granted the right to file a third-party revocation action. 2. This case meets the procedural conditions for a third-party revocation action. As creditors of Chen Lianying, Hu Bingguang and the other four could not participate as third parties in the first-instance proceedings of the original case and could not have known about the false mediation agreement reached in the second instance of the original case; they were not subjectively at fault. Upon learning of the false mediation between Chen Lianying and Jin Hengkui Company and Zhang Pingping, and the harm to their lawful rights and interests, they promptly filed the lawsuit, which did not exceed the six-month period. 3. The first-instance judgment's finding that this case meets the substantive conditions for a third-party revocation action is clear in facts and sufficient in evidence, and there is no improper situation of exceeding or substituting the trial authority of the second instance in the original case. The facts of malicious collusion between Chen Lianying, Jin Hengkui Company, and Zhang Pingping to reach a false mediation agreement are clear and well-supported. In summary, they request the dismissal of the appeal of Jin Hengkui Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong.

The facts found in the first-instance trial are supported by relevant evidence, and this court confirms them.

本院经审理认为，本案一审原告胡炳光等五人提起的系第三人撤销之诉。《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第五十六条规定： “对当事人双方的诉讼标的，第三人认为有独立请求权的，有权提起诉讼。对当事人双方的诉讼标的，第三人虽然没有独立请求权，但案件处理结果同他有法律上的利害关系的，可以申请参加诉讼，或者由人民法院通知他参加诉讼。人民法院判决承担民事责任的第三人，有当事人的诉讼权利义务。前两款规定的第三人，因不能归责于本人的事由未参加诉讼，但有证据证明发生法律效力的判决、裁定、调解书的部分或者全部内容错误，损害其民事权益的，可以自知道或者应当知道其民事权益受到损害之日起六个月内，向作出该判决、裁定、调解书的人民法院提起诉讼。人民法院经审理，诉讼请求成立的，应当改变或者撤销原判决、裁定、调解书；诉讼请求不成立的， 驳回诉讼请求。”根据上述规定，只有《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第五十六条前两款规定的有独立请求权和无独立请求权两类第三人才能作为提起第三人撤销之诉的主体。

原案系陈莲英与金恒坤公司、张平平、沈金龙之间的股权转让合同纠纷。胡炳光等五人为与陈莲英存在民间借贷关系的普通债权人。首先，就原案即陈莲英与金恒坤公司、张平平、沈金龙之间的股权转让合同纠纷而言，胡炳光等五人对原案双方当事人的诉讼标的并不享有独立请求权，其不属于《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第五十六条第一款规定的有独立请求权第三人。其次，无论原案即陈莲英与金恒坤公司、张平平、沈金龙之间的股权转让合同纠纷如何处理，其结果均不会对胡炳光等五人与陈莲英之间的民间借贷法律关系项下的权利义务产生影响。胡炳光等五人作为与陈莲英存在民间借贷关系的普通债权人，其在债权能否实现方面与原案存在一定事实上的关系，但这种事实上的联系不同于法律上的利害关系。胡炳光等五人就原案而言，亦不属于《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第五十六条第二款规定的无独立请求权第三人。

一审原告胡炳光等五人并非原案的第三人，不具备法律规定的提起第三人撤销之诉的主体资格，其起诉不符合第三人撤销之诉的受理条件。金恒坤公司、张平平、沈金龙关于胡炳光等五人不是第三人撤销之诉项下的适格原告，应驳回胡炳光等五人起诉的上诉请求成立，本院予以支持。浙江高院作出的（2013）浙商终字第63 号民事调解书如确有错误，应依法通过审判监督程序予以纠正。

综上，原审判决认定事实清楚，但适用法律错误，本院依法予以纠正。经本院审判委员会讨论决定，依照《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第五十六条、第一百五十四条第一款第三项、《最高人民法院关于适用〈中华人民共和国民事诉讼法〉的解释》第三百三十条之规定，裁定如下：

一、撤销浙江省高级人民法院（2015） 浙撤初字第1 号民事判决；

二、驳回胡炳光、胡绍料、周笃员、蒋美愈、周建光的起诉。

胡炳光预交的一审案件受理费241 800 元，胡炳光、胡绍料、周笃员、蒋美愈、周建光预交的二审案件受理费231 800 元，德清金恒坤房地产开发有限公司、张平平、沈金龙预交的二审案件受理费241 800 元，均予以退还。

本裁定为终审裁定。

二 〇 一 八 年 十 二 月 五 日

书记员  丁  一

After trial, this Court finds that the action filed by the five plaintiffs at first instance, Hu Bingguang et al., is a third-party revocation action. Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "If a third party considers that it has an independent claim to the subject matter of the action of both parties, it shall have the right to bring an action. If a third party does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the action of both parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest in it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the people's court shall notify it to participate in the proceedings. A third party for whom the people's court assumes civil liability shall have the litigation rights and obligations of a party. If a third party as specified in the preceding two paragraphs fails to participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to itself, but has evidence to prove that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement is erroneous in part or in whole, and that its civil rights and interests are harmed, it may, within six months from the date it knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were harmed, bring an action in the people's court that rendered the judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement. After trial, if the claim is established, the people's court shall amend or revoke the original judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement; if the claim is not established, the claim shall be dismissed." According to the above provisions, only the two types of third parties specified in the first two paragraphs of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, namely those with an independent claim and those without an independent claim, may be the subjects who bring a third-party revocation action.

The original case was a dispute over an equity transfer contract between Chen Lianying and Jinhuneng Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong. Hu Bingguang and the other four are ordinary creditors who had a private lending relationship with Chen Lianying. First, with respect to the original case, namely the dispute over the equity transfer contract between Chen Lianying and Jinhuneng Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, Hu Bingguang and the other four do not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation of the parties to the original case, and thus they are not third parties with an independent claim under the first paragraph of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Second, regardless of how the original case, namely the dispute over the equity transfer contract between Chen Lianying and Jinhuneng Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, is resolved, its outcome will not affect the rights and obligations under the private lending legal relationship between Hu Bingguang and the other four and Chen Lianying. As ordinary creditors who have a private lending relationship with Chen Lianying, Hu Bingguang and the other four have a de facto connection with the original case in terms of whether their claims can be realized, but such de facto connection is different from a legal interest. With respect to the original case, Hu Bingguang and the other four are also not third parties without an independent claim under the second paragraph of Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The plaintiffs at first instance, Hu Bingguang and the other four, are not third parties to the original case and do not have the standing as a subject to file a third-party revocation action as provided by law. Their lawsuit does not meet the acceptance conditions for a third-party revocation action. The appeal claims of Jinhuneng Company, Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong that Hu Bingguang and the other four are not qualified plaintiffs under the third-party revocation action and that their lawsuit should be dismissed are well-founded, and this Court supports them. If the civil mediation agreement rendered by the Zhejiang High People's Court in (2013) Zhe Shang Zhong Zi No. 63 is indeed erroneous, it should be corrected through the trial supervision procedure according to law.

In summary, the original trial found clear facts but incorrectly applied the law, and this Court corrects it according to law. After deliberation by the Judicial Committee of this Court, pursuant to Article 56, subparagraph (3) of the first paragraph of Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 330 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, it is ruled as follows:

1. The civil judgment of the Zhejiang High People's Court in (2015) Zhe Che Chu Zi No. 1 is revoked;

2. The lawsuit of Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, and Zhou Jianguang is dismissed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 241,800 prepaid by Hu Bingguang, the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 231,800 prepaid by Hu Bingguang, Hu Shaoliao, Zhou Duyuan, Jiang Meiyu, and Zhou Jianguang, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 241,800 prepaid by Deqing Jinhuneng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Zhang Pingping, and Shen Jinlong, shall all be refunded.

This ruling is final.
